races.title: State House, District 65
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Seth Woodall
cands.bio: Eden attorney who built a law practice and other businesses. Attended Rockingham Community College, UNC Greensboro and Regent University School of Law. Ran for lieutenant governor in the 2024 Republican primary. Defeated incumbent Reece Pyrtle in the 2026 primary and won House District 65 in the general election.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Woodall holding public office before this win, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, or H-1B visas. His broader statements on borders and tax cuts are too general to match to specific policies. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his stated positions come from his 2024 campaign website and a 2023 survey. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born and raised in Eden, and Ballotpedia says he was born in North Carolina; his 2023 Candidate Connection survey says he was born and raised in North Carolina and still lives in Eden.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney who grew a law practice and other businesses in Eden; has not held elected office. He ran for lieutenant governor in 2024 and lost the Republican primary.
qual.why: Law practice and business ownership fit the middle band; there is no prior legislative service or budget or policy career on record to move him higher.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2024 campaign website said he will work to make sure there is never a North Carolina law that infringes on citizens' right to keep and bear arms.

back-police-order.evidence: His 2024 campaign website said he will work to increase law enforcement funding for training, equipment and community policing.

pro-life.evidence: His 2024 campaign website said he will always fight to promote legislation to protect the lives of the unborn.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His 2024 campaign website and Candidate Connection survey said he supports school choice, so parents can decide how and where their children are educated, and wants to raise teacher pay.

cands.name: Gavin McGaughey
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 65 (Rockingham County). Graduated from Rockingham Early College High School and earned a bachelor's degree from UNC Greensboro in 2025. He has worked mostly in manufacturing and industrial construction. He has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended by the voter guide "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Gavin McGaughey was born or when he came to or settled in North Carolina. We found no record of prior elected office, a legislative or policy career, or a detailed work history beyond manufacturing and industrial construction. His campaign site has a "De-Flock Rockingham County" page and a policy page, but their text was not available, so we could not report his positions on surveillance cameras or other issues. We found no documented statements from him on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. We also found no news coverage of controversies and no notable endorsements besides one voter guide.

local.label: Roots 90: He says he is a Rockingham County public school kid and attended Rockingham Early College High School, so he was raised in North Carolina; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Manufacturing and industrial construction work; recent UNCG graduate (2025); first-time candidate with no prior elected office or legislative, policy or budget career found.
qual.why: His work record is in an occupation unrelated to lawmaking and he has no office held, so he falls in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: His work record is in an occupation unrelated to lawmaking and he has no office held, so he falls in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
